item.title: Trump and Xi Jinping will hold talks in Washington on trade, AI and more
item.description:
President Trump welcomed Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews for the Chinese leader's state visit to Washington D.C. Wednesday evening. Why it matters: U.S. presidents typically receive visiting foreign leaders at the White House, making Trump's airport welcome an unusual diplomatic gesture. The latest: Trump met Xi at the foot of the stairs after the Chinese leader's jet landed at Joint Base Andrews, the U.S. military base 13 miles southeast of the White House in Maryland. Zoom out: It's much more common for U.S. presidents to greet visiting leaders at the White House. In February 2025, Trump welcomed Volodymyr Zelensky at the West Wing entrance to kick off the Ukrainian leader's tense visit. In April of this year, King Charles III was received at the White House's South Portico. The big picture: Presidents in recent decades have occasionally greeted visiting popes at D.C.-area airports,…

item.title: What's at stake during the meeting between Trump and Xi
item.description:
Today, President Donald J. Trump and Chairman Xi Jinping are set to hold bilateral talks on trade and artificial intelligence. While this may appear to be a promising avenue for cooperation, one of the Trump administration’s top priorities should be to secure the release of political and religious prisoners held hostage by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). This concept is not purely sentiment. It is leverage. When America leads with our values instead of our shopping list, we set the terms. Defending religious freedom on American soil is how you push back against CCP transnational repression and remind Beijing that cooperation is not a blank check.
